posts.title: Training for the pass
posts.excerpt: Leg 2 climbs 180 metres. Six weeks of easy hill repeats are enough to run it without walking.
posts.content:
Once a week, find a hill that takes two minutes to run up. Run up at a pace you could still talk at, walk down, and repeat six times.

On the day, start the climb slower than feels right. The pass is long, and the descent to the sea gives the time back.

posts.title: A wider relay zone at the shrine gate
posts.excerpt: The first relay zone moves onto the gravel square this year, so teams no longer wait on the road.
posts.content:
The shrine kindly lent us the whole square. The zone is now 20 metres long and has its own water table.

Runners waiting for the sash stand behind the blue rope until a marshal calls their team number.

posts.title: The last 200 metres
posts.excerpt: Why the whole team runs the final stretch together, and how it started with one tired runner in 2015.
posts.content:
In the first year, a schoolboy on the last leg slowed to a walk near the finish. His four teammates ran out to meet him and crossed the line beside him.

Everyone cheered so loudly that it became the rule. Today every team waits at the 200-metre mark for its last runner.
